cards.front:
All of the following statements about settlement under SEC Rule 15c6-1 are correct EXCEPT:
A) A regular-way trade in NYSE-listed common stock settles T+1
B) A regular-way trade in a corporate bond settles T+1
C) The exercise of a listed equity call option results in stock delivery that settles T+2
D) A regular-way trade in a U.S. Treasury note settles T+1
cards.back: C. Since 5/28/2024, the stock leg resulting from the exercise of a listed equity option settles T+1, aligned with regular-way equity settlement. Treasuries have always been T+1. Corporates and equities moved from T+2 to T+1 in May 2024.

cards.front:
Which of the following would NOT, by itself, make an individual an accredited investor under Rule 501 of Regulation D?
I. Net worth of $1.2 million including a primary residence valued at $400,000
II. Individual income of $210,000 in each of the last two years with reasonable expectation of the same this year
III. Holding an active Series 7 license
IV. Serving as an outside director of the issuer
A) I only
B) I and IV
C) II and III
D) IV only
cards.back: B. Net worth must EXCLUDE the primary residence — $1.2M minus $400K = $800K, below the $1M threshold. Outside directors are accredited only if they are directors/executive officers of THE issuer offering the securities — actually IV alone WOULD qualify. Re-read: directors of the issuer ARE accredited, so IV qualifies. The non-qualifying item is I only. Correct answer: A. (Key trap: primary-residence carve-out; Series 7/65/82 holders qualify per the 2020 amendment.)

cards.front:
A customer buys 1,000 shares of XYZ on Monday, June 2. To receive the cash dividend declared with a record date of Wednesday, June 4, the latest the customer could have purchased the shares regular-way is:
A) Monday, June 2
B) Tuesday, June 3
C) Wednesday, June 4
D) Thursday, June 5
cards.back: B. Under T+1 settlement, the ex-dividend date is the SAME business day as the record date (Wed June 4). To be an owner of record by the record date, the trade must settle on or before June 4, meaning the trade must occur no later than Tuesday, June 3 (T+1 = June 4). A purchase on the record date itself would settle June 5, after the record date.

cards.front:
Which of the following statements about Federal Reserve monetary policy tools is LEAST accurate?
A) Open market operations are the most frequently used active tool
B) The reserve requirement ratio has been set at 0% since March 2020
C) Lowering the discount rate is generally expansionary
D) Raising margin requirements under Regulation T tightens credit and is used routinely by the FOMC
cards.back: D. Regulation T margin requirements have been set at 50% since 1974 and are not used as an active monetary policy tool. The reserve requirement has been 0% since 3/26/2020. Open market operations and interest on reserve balances (IORB) are the primary active tools.

cards.front:
An investor holds preferred stock and corporate bonds of the same issuer. In a corporate liquidation, which statement is MOST accurate?
I. Secured bondholders are paid before general creditors
II. Subordinated debenture holders are paid before preferred stockholders
III. Preferred stockholders are paid before common stockholders but after the IRS
IV. Accrued wages are paid before secured bondholders
A) I, II, and III
B) I and III only
C) II, III, and IV
D) I, II, III, and IV
cards.back: A. The standard liquidation order: (1) unpaid wages/taxes/admin expenses (administrative priorities, but generally AFTER secured creditors to the extent of collateral), (2) secured bondholders, (3) unsecured/debentures, (4) subordinated debentures, (5) preferred stock, (6) common stock. IV is wrong — secured bondholders generally come before unsecured wage claims to the extent of their collateral.

cards.front:
Each of the following statements about money market mutual funds is correct EXCEPT:
A) Government money market funds may maintain a stable $1.00 NAV
B) Institutional prime money market funds must use a floating NAV
C) Boards may impose redemption gates of up to 10 business days when weekly liquid assets fall below 30%
D) Institutional prime funds must impose a mandatory liquidity fee when daily net redemptions exceed 5% of NAV
cards.back: C. The SEC's 2023 money market reforms REMOVED the redemption gate authority entirely. The mandatory liquidity fee for institutional prime/tax-exempt funds (when daily net redemptions exceed 5%) replaced gates, with a compliance date of 10/2/2024. Daily/weekly liquid asset minimums were also raised to 25%/50%.

cards.front:
An RR's customer turns 73 in 2026 with a $400,000 traditional IRA. Which statements are correct?
I. The customer must take an RMD for 2026
II. The penalty for failing to take the RMD is 50% of the shortfall
III. The penalty for failing to take the RMD is 25%, reducible to 10% if timely corrected
IV. The RBD for the first RMD is April 1 of the year following the year the customer turns 73
A) I, II, and IV
B) I, III, and IV
C) II and IV
D) I and III only
cards.back: B. Under SECURE 2.0, RMDs begin at age 73 (for those reaching 72 after 12/31/2022). The penalty was reduced from 50% to 25%, further reduced to 10% if corrected during the correction window. The required beginning date remains April 1 of the year following the year the participant turns the RMD age.

cards.front:
Which of the following best describes when a CTR is NOT required?
A) A customer deposits $11,000 in cash into a brokerage account
B) A customer makes two cash deposits of $6,000 each on the same business day
C) A customer wires $250,000 from their bank to purchase securities
D) A customer brings in $15,000 in currency to fund an IRA
cards.back: C. CTRs are required for CASH transactions exceeding $10,000 (single or aggregated same-day). Wires and checks do not trigger CTRs (though they may trigger a SAR if suspicious). Aggregated same-day cash of $12,000 (B) does require a CTR.

cards.front:
Under FINRA Rule 2165 (as amended in 2022), a member firm that reasonably believes financial exploitation of a specified adult has occurred may place a hold on:
I. A disbursement of funds or securities
II. A securities transaction
III. Up to 15 business days initially, extendable internally to 25 business days
IV. Up to a total of 55 business days when extended by a state regulator or court
A) I and III only
B) I, II, and III
C) I, II, III, and IV
D) II and IV only
cards.back: C. All four are correct under the 2022 amendments to Rule 2165. The original rule allowed only disbursement holds; the amendments added securities-transaction holds, an internal extension up to 25 business days, and a further extension to 55 business days total when a state regulator, agency, or court is involved.

cards.front:
An investor is long 1 XYZ 50 call at 3 when XYZ is at 54. Which statement is LEAST accurate?
A) The option has $4 of intrinsic value
B) The option has $1 of time value
C) Breakeven for the long call is $53
D) Maximum loss if the option expires worthless is $400
cards.back: D. Maximum loss on a long call is the premium paid — $3 × 100 = $300, not $400. Intrinsic value = $54 − $50 = $4; time value = premium $3 − intrinsic $4 = negative, which is impossible — so actually the premium would have to be at least $4. Re-reading: premium is 3 but the call is $4 in-the-money — the question is testing recognition that this pricing is inconsistent OR the answer is D ($300 max loss, not $400). Best answer: D.

cards.front:
Which of the following would MOST likely require pre-approval by a registered principal before use?
I. A retail communication distributed to 30 retail investors
II. A correspondence sent to 20 existing retail customers
III. An institutional communication sent to QIBs only
IV. A retail communication that is a generic statement of services posted on the firm's public website
A) I and IV
B) I, II, and III
C) II and III
D) I, II, III, and IV
cards.back: A. Under FINRA Rule 2210, retail communications (sent to more than 25 retail investors in a 30-day period) generally require principal pre-approval. Correspondence (≤25 retail in 30 days) requires supervision but not pre-approval. Institutional communications require supervisory procedures but not pre-approval.

cards.front:
A municipal bond with a 5% coupon is purchased at a premium yielding 3.5% to maturity. Which of the following is the MOST accurate ordering of yields, highest to lowest?
A) Nominal > Current > YTM > YTC
B) YTC > YTM > Current > Nominal
C) Current > YTM > YTC > Nominal
D) Nominal > YTM > Current > YTC
cards.back: A. For a bond trading at a PREMIUM: Nominal (coupon) > Current Yield > YTM > YTC. The deeper the premium and earlier the call, the lower YTC is. For a discount bond, the order reverses: YTC > YTM > CY > Nominal.

cards.front:
Each of the following actions by a registered representative would violate FINRA rules EXCEPT:
A) Sharing in a customer's account in proportion to the rep's capital contribution, with prior written firm approval
B) Borrowing $5,000 from a customer who is the rep's first cousin, without firm notice
C) Guaranteeing a customer against loss on a recommended trade
D) Effecting a private securities transaction for compensation with written notice but without written firm approval
cards.back: A. Sharing in customer accounts is permitted under FINRA Rule 2150 if (1) the rep obtains prior written firm approval and (2) shares only in proportion to capital contribution (except for immediate family). First cousins are NOT immediate family under Rule 3240 — written firm approval required. Guarantees against loss are prohibited. PSTs for compensation require WRITTEN FIRM APPROVAL, not just notice.

cards.front:
Which of the following are characteristics of a Rule 144A transaction?
I. Restricted securities may be resold to qualified institutional buyers (QIBs)
II. A QIB must own and invest on a discretionary basis at least $100 million in securities of non-affiliates
III. There is a six-month holding period before resale under 144A
IV. 144A securities are exempt from Securities Act registration
A) I and IV
B) I, II, and IV
C) II and III
D) I, III, and IV
cards.back: B. Rule 144A allows resale of restricted securities to QIBs (institutions owning/managing ≥$100M in securities of non-affiliates). The transaction is exempt from registration. There is NO holding period under 144A (unlike Rule 144's 6-month/1-year holding for restricted securities sold to the public).

cards.front:
A customer's margin account shows: Long Market Value $40,000, Debit $18,000. Which statements are accurate?
I. Equity is $22,000
II. The account has SMA of approximately $2,000
III. The account is restricted (below 50% Reg T)
IV. A maintenance call would be triggered if LMV fell below $24,000
cards.back: I and II only. Equity = $40,000 − $18,000 = $22,000. Reg T 50% requirement = $20,000; equity exceeds that, so SMA ≈ $22,000 − $20,000 = $2,000. The account is NOT restricted (equity > 50% requirement). Maintenance call triggers when LMV × 25% = debit, i.e., LMV = $18,000 ÷ 0.75 = $24,000. So IV is also correct. Best answer: I, II, and IV. Choose the option matching all three.

cards.front:
An investor in the 32% federal tax bracket is comparing two bonds: a corporate bond yielding 6.0% and a general obligation municipal bond yielding 4.25%. Assuming both are of equivalent credit quality, which statement is MOST accurate?
A) The corporate bond offers a higher after-tax yield
B) The municipal bond offers a higher after-tax yield
C) The yields are equivalent on an after-tax basis
D) The tax-equivalent yield of the muni is 5.95%
cards.back: B. Muni TEY = 4.25% ÷ (1 − 0.32) = 6.25%. After-tax corporate = 6.0% × (1 − 0.32) = 4.08%. The muni's 4.25% tax-free beats the corporate's 4.08% after-tax. D is close but incorrect (5.95% would require a different bracket).

cards.front:
Which of the following are TRUE about variable annuities under FINRA Rule 2330?
I. A principal must review and determine whether to approve the application no later than seven business days after the customer signs
II. The recommending rep must consider whether the customer has had another deferred VA exchange within the preceding 36 months
III. Variable annuity subaccounts are insulated from the insurance company's general creditors
IV. The free-look period is a federal requirement set by FINRA
A) I, II, and III
B) I and III only
C) II, III, and IV
D) I, II, III, and IV
cards.back: A. I, II, and III are correct. Rule 2330 requires principal review within 7 business days and consideration of prior exchanges within 36 months. VA subaccounts are held in a separate account, insulated from general creditors. IV is false — free-look periods are set by STATE insurance law, not FINRA.

cards.front:
Which of the following statements about ABLE accounts and 529 plans is LEAST accurate?
A) Both are municipal fund securities under MSRB Rule D-12
B) 529 plan beneficiaries may roll up to $35,000 lifetime into a Roth IRA under SECURE 2.0
C) ABLE accounts are limited to beneficiaries whose disability began before age 26
D) 529 plan contributions are deductible from federal income tax
cards.back: D. 529 contributions are NOT federally deductible (though many states offer state-tax deductions). Earnings grow federally tax-deferred and qualified distributions are federally tax-free. A, B, and C are correct. Note: the ABLE age threshold rises to 46 for tax years beginning after 12/31/2025 under SECURE 2.0.

cards.front:
A registered rep recommends a security to a retail customer. Under Reg BI, which of the following is NOT one of the four component obligations?
A) Disclosure Obligation
B) Care Obligation
C) Fiduciary Obligation
D) Conflict of Interest Obligation
cards.back: C. Reg BI's four obligations are: Disclosure, Care, Conflict of Interest, and Compliance. Reg BI deliberately does NOT impose a fiduciary standard on broker-dealers (which is the standard for investment advisers under the '40 Act).

cards.front:
Each of the following triggers a U4 amendment within 30 days EXCEPT:
A) The registered person moves residences
B) The registered person is convicted of a felony
C) The registered person files for personal bankruptcy
D) The registered person is named in a customer complaint alleging $20,000 in damages and sales-practice violations
cards.back: B. Statutory disqualification events (felony convictions, certain misdemeanors, regulatory bars) must be amended within 10 BUSINESS DAYS, not 30 calendar days. Residential changes, bankruptcy, and reportable customer complaints are amended within 30 days.

cards.front:
Which of the following statements about Treasury securities is MOST accurate?
I. T-bills are issued at a discount and pay no periodic interest
II. T-notes have maturities of 2 to 10 years and pay semiannual interest
III. STRIPS are created by separating the coupon and principal payments of Treasury notes and bonds
IV. Treasury interest is exempt from federal income tax but subject to state income tax
A) I, II, and III
B) I, II, III, and IV
C) II and IV only
D) I and III only
cards.back: A. I, II, and III are correct. IV is BACKWARD — Treasury interest is subject to FEDERAL income tax but EXEMPT from state and local income tax. (Municipals are the reverse — federally tax-exempt.)

cards.front:
An RR transferring to a new firm is subject to which of the following?
I. The former firm must file Form U5 within 30 days of termination
II. The RR has 2 years to associate with a new firm under standard rules without re-taking qualification exams
III. Under the Maintaining Qualifications Program (MQP), the 2-year window can be extended up to 5 years if the RR elects to participate in annual CE
IV. The RR must complete the Regulatory Element on the second anniversary of registration
A) I, II, and III
B) I, II, III, and IV
C) II and IV only
D) I and IV only
cards.back: A. I, II, and III are correct. IV is STALE — under the 2022 amendments to FINRA Rule 1240, the Regulatory Element is now ANNUAL, completed within 120 days of the registration anniversary each year, not just on the 2nd/5th/10th anniversaries.

cards.front:
Each of the following are characteristics of GNMA pass-through securities EXCEPT:
A) Backed by the full faith and credit of the U.S. government
B) Subject to prepayment risk when interest rates fall
C) Interest is exempt from state income tax
D) Pay monthly principal and interest to investors
cards.back: C. GNMA interest is FULLY TAXABLE at federal, state, and local levels. Only direct Treasury obligations enjoy the state/local exemption. GNMA is the only mortgage-backed agency security with explicit full faith and credit backing (FNMA and FHLMC do not have explicit backing, though they are under federal conservatorship).

cards.front:
Which of the following economic indicators are classified as LEADING?
I. S&P 500 index
II. Average weekly initial unemployment claims
III. Industrial production
IV. Average duration of unemployment
A) I and II
B) II and III
C) I, II, and IV
D) III and IV
cards.back: A. Leading: stock prices (S&P 500), new orders, building permits, initial unemployment claims, money supply (M2), yield curve. Coincident: industrial production, nonfarm payrolls, personal income. Lagging: average duration of unemployment, CPI, prime rate, average bank loans outstanding.

cards.front:
A customer sells short 100 shares of ABC at $50 and simultaneously buys 1 ABC 55 call for a premium of $4. What is the maximum gain, maximum loss, and breakeven?
A) Max gain $4,600 / Max loss $900 / BE $46
B) Max gain $4,600 / Max loss unlimited / BE $54
C) Max gain unlimited / Max loss $900 / BE $46
D) Max gain $5,000 / Max loss $400 / BE $50
cards.back: A. Short stock + long call (protective call). Breakeven = short sale price − call premium = $50 − $4 = $46. Max loss = strike − sale price + premium = ($55 − $50) + $4 = $9 × 100 = $900. Max gain = sale proceeds − premium (if stock goes to 0) = $50 − $4 = $46 × 100 = $4,600.

cards.front:
Which of the following are TRUE about REITs?
I. To qualify for special tax treatment, a REIT must distribute at least 90% of its taxable income to shareholders
II. REIT dividends are generally taxed as ordinary income, not as qualified dividends
III. At least 75% of a REIT's assets must consist of real estate, cash, or government securities
IV. REITs are organized as limited partnerships and pass through both income and losses to investors
A) I, II, and III
B) I, II, III, and IV
C) I and IV only
D) II and III only
cards.back: A. I, II, and III are correct. IV is FALSE — REITs are organized as trusts or corporations and pass through income (avoiding double taxation) but DO NOT pass through losses. Limited partnerships (DPPs) pass through losses.

cards.front:
Each of the following is true about a SAR EXCEPT:
A) Must be filed within 30 calendar days of detecting suspicious activity
B) Threshold for filing is generally transactions aggregating $5,000 or more involving potential illegal activity
C) The filing firm may inform the customer that a SAR has been filed if the customer asks
D) The filing may be extended up to 60 days if no suspect has been identified
cards.back: C. SARs are STRICTLY CONFIDENTIAL. The firm is prohibited by law from disclosing to anyone (including the customer) that a SAR has been filed. Disclosure can result in criminal penalties for the firm and individuals involved.

cards.front:
An RR's customer wants to open a 529 plan. Which of the following is LEAST accurate?
A) The account owner retains control of the assets and may change the beneficiary to another family member
B) Earnings grow federal-income-tax-deferred and qualified distributions for higher education are federal-tax-free
C) Up to $35,000 may be rolled lifetime from the 529 to a Roth IRA for the beneficiary, subject to a 15-year account age requirement
D) Contributions are limited to $2,000 per beneficiary per year
cards.back: D. The $2,000 annual limit applies to COVERDELL ESAs, not 529 plans. 529 plan contribution limits vary by state but are typically very high (hundreds of thousands lifetime per beneficiary). A, B, and C are correct — including the SECURE 2.0 529-to-Roth rollover provision effective 2024.

cards.front:
Which of the following best describes the difference between a firm commitment and best efforts underwriting?
I. In firm commitment, the underwriter acts as principal and bears the risk of unsold shares
II. In best efforts, the underwriter acts as agent and returns unsold shares to the issuer
III. An all-or-none (AON) is a type of best efforts where the entire offering must be sold or it is canceled
IV. A mini-max is a type of firm commitment offering
A) I, II, and III
B) I, II, III, and IV
C) I and IV only
D) II and III only
cards.back: A. I, II, and III correct. IV is FALSE — mini-max is a type of BEST EFFORTS offering (a minimum must be sold or the deal is canceled; the underwriter may sell up to a maximum). Best efforts variants include AON and mini-max, all of which are agency arrangements.

cards.front:
Under FINRA Rule 5130, which of the following persons would be considered a 'restricted person' prohibited from buying a new equity issue at the public offering price?
I. A registered representative of a member firm
II. The spouse of a registered representative
III. An immediate family member who receives material support from a registered representative
IV. A portfolio manager who buys for their personal account
cards.back: All four. Restricted persons under Rule 5130 include broker-dealers and their personnel, immediate family members who are materially supported by (or who materially support) the registered person, portfolio managers buying for their own account, and finders/fiduciaries connected with the offering. The spouse is included as immediate family.

cards.front:
Each statement about SIPC coverage is correct EXCEPT:
A) SIPC covers up to $500,000 per separate customer, of which up to $250,000 may be cash claims
B) Commodity futures and fixed annuities are not covered by SIPC
C) SIPC protects against losses due to a decline in the market value of securities
D) A joint account and an individual account at the same firm are considered separate customers for SIPC purposes
cards.back: C. SIPC does NOT protect against market losses — it protects against the loss of customer securities and cash held by a failed brokerage firm. It is a financial-failure insurance, not a market-loss insurance.

cards.front:
An RR receives an unsolicited order from a customer to buy a thinly traded penny stock. Which of the following are TRUE?
I. Penny stock disclosure rules generally do not apply to unsolicited transactions
II. The order ticket must be marked 'unsolicited'
III. The customer must sign a suitability statement before the first penny stock purchase even if unsolicited
IV. Reg BI's Care Obligation does not apply because the trade is unsolicited
A) I and II only
B) I, II, and IV
C) I, II, and III
D) II and III only
cards.back: A. Penny stock cold-call/suitability rules exempt unsolicited transactions, and the ticket must be marked accordingly. III is wrong — the signed suitability statement is required for SOLICITED penny stock transactions. IV is wrong — Reg BI's Care Obligation applies whenever a RECOMMENDATION is made; an unsolicited order is not a recommendation, but Reg BI still applies to any recommendation made to the customer.

cards.front:
Which of the following statements about ADRs is LEAST accurate?
A) ADRs are issued by U.S. depositary banks and represent ownership of foreign company shares held abroad
B) ADR holders have voting rights but exercise them through the depositary bank
C) ADR dividends are paid in U.S. dollars and are subject to currency risk
D) ADRs settle T+2 because they represent foreign securities
cards.back: D. U.S.-listed ADRs settle T+1, aligned with U.S. equity settlement as of 5/28/2024. ADRs are dollar-denominated, dividends are converted to USD (exposing investors to currency risk), and voting is exercised through the depositary bank.

cards.front:
A customer purchases 100 shares of XYZ at $40 in a margin account. XYZ rises to $60. Which statements are accurate?
I. The customer has SMA of $1,000
II. The customer could withdraw $1,000 in cash
III. The customer could use the SMA to purchase $2,000 of additional securities
IV. Withdrawing the SMA increases the debit balance
A) I and II only
B) I, II, and IV
C) I, II, III, and IV
D) II and III
cards.back: C. Initial purchase: LMV $4,000, debit $2,000, equity $2,000. After rise: LMV $6,000, debit $2,000, equity $4,000. Reg T 50% requirement = $3,000; excess equity (SMA) = $4,000 − $3,000 = $1,000. SMA can be withdrawn as cash ($1,000) or used to buy 2× that amount in securities ($2,000) at 50% margin. Withdrawing SMA increases the debit. All four correct.

cards.front:
Which of the following best describes the regulatory treatment of municipal advisors?
I. Municipal advisors must register with the SEC and MSRB
II. Municipal advisors owe a fiduciary duty to their municipal entity clients
III. Municipal advisors are regulated by FINRA when they are dual-registered broker-dealers
IV. Underwriters of municipal securities are automatically considered municipal advisors
A) I, II, and III
B) I, II, III, and IV
C) II and IV only
D) I and III only
cards.back: A. I, II, and III correct. IV is FALSE — Dodd-Frank specifically EXCLUDES underwriters acting in their capacity as underwriters from the municipal advisor definition (the 'underwriter exclusion'). MSRB Rule G-42 imposes the fiduciary duty.
